note: Memory bandwidth and capacity for devices that run models locally. Single-
stream decode is bandwidth bound, so bandwidth is the number that decides
throughput and compute is usually irrelevant.
Bandwidth figures for Apple parts are as reported alongside the measurements
in the llama.cpp Apple Silicon benchmark thread, which is also the source of
the validation set. Adding a device means adding a real source, not a
recollection: a spec table invented by a language model is worse than no
tool, because it is confidently wrong exactly where the user cannot check.

sources.jetson: NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano Super, 8 GB LPDDR5

m3.name: Apple M3
m3.caution: No measurement for the base M3 in the validation set. The estimate rests on the model, not on a measured point for this part.

m3-max.name: Apple M3 Max
m3-max.caution: Reported as 300-400 GB/s depending on configuration. 350 is the midpoint.

pi5.name: Raspberry Pi 5
pi5.caution: Processor only. There is no accelerator path for large language models on this board: the AI HAT's Hailo part runs compiled vision networks, not language models.
